influences.name: Phil Spector
influences.context: Wilson was inspired by the concept of extrasensory perception, Phil Spector's production of "You've Lost That Lovin' Feelin'", and recreational drugs, possibly including LSD, in creating the song.

influences.name: George Gershwin
influences.context: Biographer Peter Ames Carlin believed Wilson viewed the song as "a smaller, psychedelic version" of George Gershwin's Rhapsody in Blue.

influences.name: the Crystals
influences.context: Wilson likened the cello triplets to a similar effect in the Crystals' "Da Doo Ron Ron" (1963).

influences.name: the Dell-Vikings
influences.context: Wilson likened Love's singing to the bass vocal on the Dell-Vikings' "Come Go with Me"

influences.name: Wilson Pickett
influences.context: Mike Love's first impression of "Good Vibrations" was that it sounded like the "very heavy R&B" associated with singer Wilson Pickett.

influences.name: Chuck Berry
influences.context: The song, heavily influenced by Chuck Berry's "Sweet Little Sixteen," became an anthem for the surf rock genre.
